title: Unquoted attribute value containing a comma
message: Attribute values containing `,` must be quoted. Write `widths="1,3"` rather than `widths=1,3`.
hints: Some extension READMEs (for example pandoc-ext/list-table's `aligns=l,c`) write these values unquoted; add the quotes when copying them.

cases.name: div
cases.description: A comma-separated value on a fenced div, as in pandoc-ext/list-table's `widths=1,3`. Recovery consumes the div, so its closing `:::` and every later fence used to be reported as further parse errors; `desynchronizes` drops them. Every unquoted value with a character the attribute lexer rejects (`,`, `;`, `(`, `<`, ...) fails in this one state, so the case is guarded on a comma appearing in the value: the others keep the generic error rather than a message about commas.

cases.name: span
cases.description: The same value on a bracketed span. Attribute specifiers on spans, images, inline code and headings all reach the div's state; this case and the heading case document that rather than claiming anything new.

cases.name: heading
cases.description: The same value on a heading attribute.
